Improves on L4D formula in almost every way. 

 Card system adds increased replay-ability through the variety of level modifiers (corruption cards) and through the deck building system . Gunplay feels modern and satisfying with addition of ADS  and weapon customization.  There is a much larger variety of weapons and items that all feel useful in their own way. Map design is solid with a typically much more open design with "stash houses" and items randomly positioned around the level giving a reason to stop and explore certain areas. The game has a lot more flavor than L4D however I'm not sure it is all up to the same quality. The overarching story told through the campaign is fine but certainly not the main attraction here. I enjoyed some of the concepts and the sense of cohesion all of the acts have but wouldve enjoy a little bit more variety in the setting.  
I havent tried the PvP and probably never will.

Overall I'm not really sure what more you could want out of a spiritual successor to L4D2.

Honestly its really hard for me to rate this game so poorly. 
The game is extremely rough and feels like a Beta Test. 
That being said the game also looks great but doesn't feel so great. 

The Storyline is not a thing.. like at all, you go through a series of missions but none of them feel different from the previous mission you completed. 
With the stroyline, the weapons are nice but once an attachment is on the weapon, you cannot simply remove it, you have to find another attachment and replace it. even if your weapon attachment is broken which causes negative affects to game play.  
The weapons are nice but its hard to tell what is better and if something is better you cannot move over your hard earned attachments.. you have to find all new ones for this new weapon... huge flaw. 

The Deck System is Alright... Its very convoluted, there are two systems 
Campaign Decks - These cards are alright and will help you through, if you make a deck make sure it has all 15 cards or you will just get fed Pre-generated cards that arent good. 

Versus Decks - These decks are nice and can be meta gamed a bit nothing negative to be said here. 

However through the pipeline unlock system in which you get these cards. The system doesn't tell you which cards your saving to unlock go where, therefor you have to guess if you're unlocking a card for Campaign or for Versus. This can cause you to sink a ton of currency into something not knowing the outcome of it. 

The AI in the Campaign are basically non-existent, they'll watch you die and do nothing or rather just soak dmg from the zombies. thats it. 

- Versus Mode (PvP)- 

There is currently only one game mode in the game, you alternate between being infected and being cleaners. the rounds are extremely short averaging 3-4 minutes for better pre made comps and 1-2 minutes for randoms. 
Leaving games causes you to have a 5 minute sit out period however if your team leaves no one can rejoin the game to help you. if everyone on the opposing team leaves.. you dont get anything for that game. it just sends you back to the lobby... 
if you pre make a team theres a very good chance you'll win every single game, just due to how the infected work and how teamwork is in this game. the meta is basically tall-boys and reekers = wins. 


In conclusion, the game is a solid 5.5/10. Its beautiful however at what cost? $60 for an unfinished game with unfinished systems, broken mechanics and animations that plain dont work.

I also noticed there is no happy medium in between the easiest difficulty (Recruit) up to the medium (Veteran). Recruit is too easy. Veteran feels like you are playing at a level that is impossible at times. I have not yet played Nightmare (the highest difficulty).  But I am assuming it is insane compared to the already difficult medium. Other than that, the only thing that this game is missing is allowing you to remove attachments from weapons to make it easier swapping attachments or maintaining the attachments you have acquired using a previous weapon.

Don't get me wrong, it is a good game but still has some major flaws, i would not recommend it at the current state for its price tag.
There are bugs, not making the game unplayable but making it feel unfinished. One thing that happens to me frequently is throwing a grenade and ending up with no hands, the character does not re-equip a weapon automatically.
The team bots are stupid, hands down stupid. They heal you the wrong time(e.g. after taking pills), do not heal themselves with healing kits you point out to them, do not take initiative to shoot to specials close to them, frequently fail to prioritize reviving a player rather than running around doing things.
Special infected spawns on higher difficulty is random, TOO random. I've ended un having 3 specials in a room and getting my ass whooped.
While the card system for upgrades is a nice feature, i feel that the game needed a level up/ranking system.
I've played and played normal mode with players on their first playthrough and the game used us to clean the pavement. Failing to provide a ranking/level system means players will throw themselves on higher difficulties and make the community salty about how everyone sucks at the game. While i tolerate helping other players, i am tired of being stuck in the first level of the campaign on higher difficulties because players don't even know things like the bird mechanic.
One thing that i feel is really stupid is the absence a kick function. I've been in games with toxic players, but the major issue is afk people, people taking ages to start games. You can either report them(which is too drastical for the case) or wait and get frustrated.
I am not aware on how the game runs or feels on console, but seeing the performance of console players vs pc players i can tell it is definitely harder to play on console. Also console players take a lot more to join.
Again, it is a good game, but i feel it should have been tested internally better.
If you plan to release a successor to a major success like the left4dead franchise the stakes are much higher than releasing a generic zombie game.
Please developers keep testing and fixing things because there is a lot of potential, but some things are really REALLY frustrating.
